text:
Bridgeport had 6 licensed child care facilities in 2025, state data shows
H. I. Willis
Bridgeport reported 6 licensed child care providers in 2025, according to the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services.
Among these facilities, 1 was classified as a day care center (16.7%), 4 as group day care homes (66.7%), and 1 as a family child care home (16.7%).
Bridgeport's providers accommodate various age groups, ranging from birth to 12 years, 6 weeks to 12 years, and 3 years to 5 years.
All child care facilities in Bridgeport offer services in English.
Across Illinois, there were 8,602 licensed child care facilities in 2025.
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services suspended certain federal child care and family assistance payments for California, Colorado, Minnesota, New York and Illinois due to concerns regarding fraud and misuse, the agency announced Jan. 6. This action withholds nearly $2.4 billion in Child Care and Development Fund grants, $7.35 billion in Temporary Assistance for Needy Families funds and $869 million in Social Services Block Grants, requiring states to provide documentation before continuing payments.
Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker called the move “wrong and cruel” and indicated the state could challenge the freeze, stressing that Illinois already has anti‑fraud measures in place.
The Illinois administration estimates the freeze could impact about 100,000 families and more than 152,000 children who participate in the state’s Child Care Assistance Program, along with funding for thousands of licensed child care providers and 275 human service organizations.
